content: Obesity is a risk factor for the development of several cancers, including breast, colon, and gynecologic carcinomas.1,2 Recently, it has become clear that obesity not only correlates with carcinogenesis but also influences the prognosis of patients with several types of cancer. For example, obesity has been associated with poor prognosis in breast3,4 and colon cancers,5,6 whereas favorable prognoses have been reported in obese patients with gastric7 or renal8 cancers.
